newsitem.title: USA: Natural gas, electric market convergence growing.
newsitem.headline: Natural gas, electric market convergence growing.

text.p: The trend of convergence between the natural gas and electric industries--at both the commodity and corporate level--is picking up speed, industry experts said Tuesday.
Attending an Edison Electric Institute conference, Dan Ryser, vice president at Electric Clearinghouse Inc., said the focus is on managing "energy" rather than a specific generation source.
"This is one very large, very complicated energy business," he said.

The trend has led to the development of futures contracts, tolling contracts, commodity swaps and "energy" sales with an option to deliver either megawatts or gas and to the formation of national integrated market players, noted Ryser.
Thomas Flaherty, a partner at Deloitte & Touche Consulting Group, said he expects to see more alliances and mergers between electric utilities and natural gas distributors.
He cited propsed ventures between Boston Gas and Eastern Energy as well as Southern California Gas and Enova as evidence of this growing trend.
"Electric providers are available," Flaherty said. "The market is searching for partners."
He predicted that the most successful utilities will pursue "super-regional" status by moving quickly to lock up customers with a total package of energy services.
"You can't expect to make a living just by brokering power. You have to add value," said NGC's Ryser.
